speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong
text: asked the Minister for Health whether there is a crunch in the specialised transportation of seniors to care centres and, if so, how is this affecting the placement of seniors in these centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This ensures that clients can access the care services they need.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Centres can tap on a range of transport options to serve their clients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: AIC also works with taxi operators and private hire car operators to expand the range of transport services available to centres.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: From time-to-time, some centres may encounter short-term challenges in accessing transport services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For example, some centres may take more time to purchase and modify a van or to enter into arrangements with their preferred transport operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: When any centre faces transport difficulties, we encourage them to inform us and AIC will work with them to find alternative transport arrangements so that there is minimal impact on client placement.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Speaker, I thank the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The first one is regarding the AIC's centralised transport service.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In your view, is there any supply crunch right now in providing the specialised vans and going into the future where there is an extension of the eldercare centres?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second question is with regard to the collaboration between AIC and the taxi operators and the private hire companies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is the scope of the collaboration beyond just in terms of teaching the drivers how to handle wheelchair-bound commuters?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is it more than just that in terms of expanding the fleet, for example, into specialised vans and a more direct kind of collaboration between homes and the companies?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Even if the demand increases, centres can activate committed capacity under the AIC centralised transport service or other specialised transport operators or use private hire cars, such as GrabAssist and taxis, as an interim approach.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As to the Member's supplementary question on the collaboration between GrabAssist or with taxis, other than training the taxi drivers on how to handle such clients, if need be, should there be capacity for specialised vans that can be provided by these operators, I think we can also extend that collaboration to them as well.
